zhanggui-requesting-code-review: Runs a new independent review of a diff or code change and reports Critical and Important findings by severity. Use when a diff, patch, or code change needs a new independent review, including a severity-scoped report of Critical and Important findings, before verification, merge, delivery, or dependent work starts, even when the change looks small.
zhanggui-verification-before-completion: Proves a completion claim with fresh evidence — real command output, test results, an actual run — before anyone acts on it. Use when work is about to be called complete, fixed, passing, or ready, or before a commit, push, pull request, or handoff to the next task, and no fresh evidence for that claim has been produced yet, even when the change looks obviously safe.
zhanggui-finishing-a-development-branch: Closes out verified branch or worktree work with one explicit decision — merge, open a pull request, keep the branch, or discard it. Use when branch or worktree work has already passed verification and needs an explicit decision about how to land it, such as merging, opening a pull request, keeping the branch, or discarding it, including right after the user says the tests passed, even if they never mention merging or a pull request.
zhanggui-using-git-worktrees: Creates an isolated git worktree for feature work so the main working tree stays untouched, including setup and later cleanup. Use when feature work needs an isolated checkout, a write scope separated from the main working tree, or a dedicated workspace for executing an implementation plan, even if the request never says 'worktree'.
zhanggui-dispatching-parallel-agents: Runs independent pieces of work at the same time instead of one after another, keeping one writer per file set. Use when subagent capacity is available and two or more independent problem domains can run at the same time on non-overlapping files without shared state, such as separate root-cause investigations in different components or dependency-ready tasks with distinct write scopes, even when the request only lists several things to do.
setup-collaboration-files: Initializes or normalizes a project's collaboration file system — rule files, architecture docs, decision notes, and status files. Use when a project needs its collaboration file system (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md, docs/, .agents/notes/, tools.md, memory.md) initialized or normalized, including when the user asks to "init project", "set up AGENTS.md", "initialize collaboration files" or "normalize rules", and when work starts on an unfamiliar project that lacks structured collaboration files, whether greenfield or with existing rule files to unify.
decision-notes: Records the reasoning behind code that looks deliberately odd — which alternatives were rejected, why, and what each decision cost. Use when a non-trivial change, upgrade, incident fix, or abandoned attempt needs its reasoning recorded for the next session, including when someone asks to write a decision note or explain why the code is deliberately shaped this way, when an option that was already rejected is proposed again, or when a superseded decision must be preserved instead of rewritten.
